html:
The Franco-Hova Wars were the French campaigns of 1883 to 1885 and 1894 to 1895 that conquered the Merina kingdom, ending with the annexation of Madagascar as a French colony in August 1896.

The first war gave France a protectorate and the port of Diego Suarez. In 1895 a French army landed on the west coast and marched inland, losing thousands of men to disease, and shelled Antananarivo into surrender in September.

A popular revolt followed. General Gallieni crushed it, abolished the monarchy in 1897 and exiled Queen Ranavalona III. French rule brought forced labour, a head tax and land grants to settlers, and the uprising of 1947 was its sharpest challenge. It ended the Merina state built since Andrianampoinimerina.
